findings.issue: OPAQUE-FRACTION BAND CONTRADICTION (the headline gap). W08's blob gate asserts a contained opaque-fraction band of 0.25-0.60 (25-60%), and AX.md §3 line 643 agrees (0.25-0.6). But W00's shared `proof:substrate-paints-color` floor — which W08 EXPLICITLY composes ('composes the W00 proof:substrate-paints-color readPixels primitive (the shared non-black/contained-band floor)') — asserts a band of 'roughly 10-45%' (W00 lines 32, 114). The audit measured 84.1% coverage at HEAD with a ~1.34x footprint, so the contained target (~84.1/1.34 ≈ 0.63) sits ABOVE W00's 45% ceiling. W00's floor is the wrong/too-tight one, and it is the shared primitive both W07 and W08 build on. In an autonomous run this is a hard stall: the implementer tunes the blob to W08's 25-60% band, the W00-owned shared-floor gate goes RED, and two waves' gates carry conflicting authorities with no reconciliation note in §4.

W00 owns the SHARED floor; it must widen its blob band to encompass W08's tuned target (the contained droplet at ~0.25-0.65), OR W00's floor must be a loose non-flood/non-blank sanity bound (e.g. 0.10 < frac < 0.70) and W08's gate carries the TIGHT contained band (0.25-0.6) as its own parity assertion. findings.issue: W07 GATE IS METAL-BACKEND-BLIND TO DEFECT 1b ON CI (the real-device GO criterion is only half load-bearing headless). W07 fix has TWO independent defects: 1a (int-in-float, backend-universal) and 1b (var<uniform> dynamic-index miscompile that reproduces ONLY 'on Apple/Metal (Tint→Metal codegen)'). The adversarial-verify step itself says 'reverts ONLY the storage move ... confirms the gate STILL goes RED on Metal' — i.e. 1b's load-bearing-ness is provable ONLY on a Metal backend. But W00's recommended device choice is Chrome-headless-new (W00 line 82), and Chrome WebGPU on Linux CI runs over Vulkan/SwiftShader, which correctly handles var<uniform> dynamic indexing — so on non-Metal CI the gate goes GREEN with ONLY fix 1a applied. The headless `proof:aurora-webgpu-render` cannot independently catch a 1b-only regression on a non-Metal autonomous runner. The spec names the dev-Mac live audit (Metal) as the binding close criterion, which DOES catch 1b, but never flags that the CI gate is backend-blind to 1b — an autonomous agent running CI on Linux would wrongly believe the gate proves both fixes.
findings.fix: Add an explicit backend-coverage note to W07's HardGate + Cadence: 'The storage-transposition fix (1b) is Metal-codegen-specific; the headless gate proves it as load-bearing ONLY on a Metal/Tint backend. On a non-Metal CI runner (SwiftShader/Vulkan) the gate proves 1a (counts) + the WebGL2-vs-WebGPU delta but NOT 1b — 1b is caught by the per-i32-field decode + the dev-Mac VISUAL-TRUTH live audit. The W00 device-choice manifest MUST record whether the runner is Metal-capable; if not, the live audit on a Metal machine is the BINDING 1b GO criterion, not the CI gate.' This makes the real-device GO criterion honest about which backend proves which defect.

findings.issue: W07 HAS NO CI-DEVICE-ABSENT DISPOSITION (fail-CLOSED vs befitting-silent ambiguity at the device boundary). W07's gate REQUIRES a real GPUDevice. findings.issue: W13's close criterion ("stunning / congruent to actual Van Gogh works") is NOT operationalized into anything an autonomous agent can check or self-assess. The HardGate's three headless gates (proof:aurora-vangogh-preset, -oilpastel-medium, -stroke-composite) are all SOURCE-PARSE/STRUCTURE proofs (passthrough-absent, distinct-function, OKLab-not-linear-mix) — they prove the CODE shape changed, not that the painted image is stunning. The only forward 'is it beautiful' assertion is the VISUAL-TRUTH live audit, which is a subjective human 'frontend-design pass ... audited AGAINST actual Van Gogh (Starry Night swirl-row dabs) / oil-pastel reference works.' In a 12-hour unattended autonomous run there is no human, and the spec gives the agent no executable way to render the side-by-side, no committed reference image, and no pass/fail proxy. A first-class van-Gogh body and the HEAD passthrough oil BOTH pass every headless gate-that-can-run-autonomously plus the π-lane non-black floor — so 'stunning' is unfalsifiable by the autonomous lane. This is the exact cardinal-AW failure class (green structure over an un-validated render) re-entering at the painterly layer.
findings.fix: Operationalize 'stunning/congruent' into the EXACT computable image-statistic laws the wave's own research corpus already states, and add them as π-lane numeric assertions on the readback (autonomous-executable, no human, no committed copyrighted reference). The corpus supplies the exact laws: (a) ATOMICITY — van-Gogh must read as separable dabs with inter-stroke canvas gaps: assert a measurable high-frequency gap-fraction / local-contrast floor on the vangogh readback that the oil passthrough's continuous coverage field FAILS (the falsifiable van-Gogh-vs-oil discriminator). (b) NO-FLAT-FILLS — assert a within-region value-variance floor (aurora-synthesis.md:36, aurora-README.md:341 'within-region value variation via pigment-density turbulence'); a flat stamped-swatch render falls below it. (c) OVERLAP-NOT-GREY — assert OKLab hue-angle preservation across a dense van-Gogh complementary-overlap region (chroma does NOT collapse toward neutral); the linear-mix HEAD render reds it (this is the slice-8-F2 'single highest-leverage lever' made numeric). (d) STARRY-NIGHT TURBULENCE — optionally assert the readback's radial luminance power-spectrum slope sits in the −5/3 Kolmogorov band the corpus names (aurora-README.md:128, synthesis:111) as the swirl-row congruence proxy. Each is a deterministic statistic over the π-lane pixels, gives the autonomous agent a falsifiable close, and the human frontend-design audit stays the ADDITIONAL bar when a human is present — not the SOLE one.

findings.issue: W13 names 'actual Van Gogh / oil-pastel reference works' as the comparison target 8+ times but never names WHERE they live — no fixture path, no committed asset under tests-visual/, no URL. An autonomous agent cannot fetch a reference (offline 12-hour run, and committing Van Gogh reproductions raises a copyright/asset question the spec never addresses). The 'side-by-side against a Starry Night reference' and the 'per-medium texture-snapshot delta against the Van Gogh / oil-pastel reference works' are thus un-runnable as written.
findings.fix: Replace the 'against actual reference works' framing with a self-referential checkable bar: the reference is the STATISTICAL TARGET (the atomicity/variance/overlap/power-spectrum bands of finding 1), not a copyrighted image the agent must hold. State explicitly that the live human side-by-side against Van Gogh works is the HUMAN-PRESENT enrichment, and the AUTONOMOUS close criterion is (i) the three structure gates GREEN + (ii) the new π-lane painterly-statistic assertions GREEN + (iii) the paired-π BEFORE/AFTER+DELTA capture showing the named statistics MOVED in the right direction vs the HEAD passthrough baseline. If a public-domain reference fixture is wanted, name a specific one (Starry Night is public domain — pre-1929) and commit it to tests-visual/fixtures/ with a provenance note, so the comparison is reproducible rather than aspirational.

findings.issue: The 'per-medium texture-snapshot gates' (charter §3) are de-fanged to a bare capture in W13: 'rides the π-lane readback, NOT a CPU text gate alone' and 'captures a per-medium texture snapshot ... so each medium's distinct character is pixel-evidenced.' A capture that is only eyeballed is not a gate — it has no assertion, no tolerance, no RED condition. The DELTA artefact is a compare-at-close human read, not a machine threshold. So the 'per-medium texture' arm cannot fail autonomously even when vangogh==oil-pastel==crayon all render identically.
findings.fix: Turn the per-medium texture snapshot into an assertion: require the pairwise readback distance between {vangogh, oil-pastel, crayon, oil} to exceed a threshold (each medium is MEASURABLY distinct from the other three over a fixed region) — a deterministic 'four media are not the same picture' check that the HEAD shared-body state (oil-pastel≡crayon, vangogh≡oil) fails. This directly machine-proves the wave's headline ('two materially-different media are not one dispatch body') at the PIXEL layer, complementing the source-structure proof that they are not one FUNCTION.

slices.notes:
Net assessment: W10-W14 are structurally among the most rigorous waves in the tranche — born-RED witnesses with exact GLSL line refs, source-parse/deletion-proof gates that are precept-valid, W12's twin-equivalence substrate carve, and W14's EXCISE-vs-WIRE fork carrying exact Kuwahara constants (Kyprianidis 2009 polynomial soft-blend, η≈0.1/λ≈0.5, hardness≈8) PLUS the sharp pre-2010 hard-argmin pinwheel warning. W14's 'stunning' is honestly deferred-by-design (EXCISE = no painterly WebGPU finish), which is sound.

The ONE real gap, and it is the exact question this slice was assigned: 'stunning / congruence to actual Van Gogh works' (W13) is NOT operationalized into a checkable autonomous bar. The wave's entire forward 'is-it-beautiful' close rests on a subjective human frontend-design audit against un-named, un-committed 'reference works' — un-executable in a 12-hour unattended run, and the headless gates that CAN run autonomously (structure/deletion proofs + the π-lane non-black floor) all pass for BOTH the HEAD passthrough oil AND a first-class van-Gogh body. So an autonomous agent has no falsifiable signal that distinguishes stunning from merely non-black. This is the cardinal-AW failure class (green structure over an un-validated render) re-entering at the painterly layer — precisely what AX exists to close.

The fix is in-hand and low-risk: the wave's OWN research corpus (aurora-README.md / aurora-synthesis.md) already states the computable laws — atomicity/inter-stroke-gap, no-flat-fills within-region variance floor, OKLab overlap-not-grey hue/chroma preservation, the −5/3 Kolmogorov swirl-row power spectrum. Routing those into a new π-lane numeric gate (proof:aurora-painterly-statistics) converts 'stunning' from aspiration into a deterministic, RED-at-HEAD/GREEN-on-fix assertion, with the human side-by-side preserved as the human-present enrichment tier rather than the sole bar. The concreteEdits add that gate, dual-tier the close criterion, name a public-domain Starry Night fixture, harden the strokeMode:crayon clean-break against a silent consumer no-op, give W14 an autonomous-default fallthrough, and surface the §2.4 deferral at charter level. With these, the slice drives end-to-end unattended.

Verdict needs-sharpening (not has-gap): the structural scaffolding is complete and correct; what's missing is the numeric operationalization of the qualitative bar, which the corpus already supplies — a sharpening, not a hole in the architecture.

findings.issue: W17 'no light-dark()' static gate has a TRANSITIVE-var hole that re-admits the cardinal Canvas2D defect. proof:constellation-tokens clause (c) only forbids (1) the literal `light-dark(` substring inside a `--constellation-*` declaration and (2) `--constellation-line == var(--foreground)`. But the library's ENTIRE neutral ladder is light-dark(): tokens.css:1387-1392 defines `--neutral-0..6: light-dark(...)`, and `--foreground`/`--background` resolve through it. The slides code falls back to `var(--neutral-4)`/`var(--neutral-3)` as the 'neutral default' — so an implementer authoring the natural `--constellation-node: var(--neutral-4)` (or `var(--background)`, `var(--card)`, etc.) PASSES the static substring check yet resolves to a light-dark() value at runtime → Canvas2D silently rejects it → the exact W30 86.3%-red-splatter defect reappears at the library layer. The gate must catch transitive light-dark() references, not just the literal substring.
findings.fix: Strengthen proof:constellation-tokens clause (c): forbid ANY `var(` reference inside a `--constellation-*` declaration (the tokens must be literal `hsl()`/hex plain-hsl, never `var(--neutral-*)`/`var(--foreground)`/`var(--background)`/`var(--card)`), OR resolve the referenced token transitively and assert it contains no `light-dark(`. The simplest fail-closed rule (and the one the 'PLAIN-hsl by construction' intent already implies): a `--constellation-*` value matching `/var\(/` is RED unless it references another already-validated plain-hsl `--constellation-*` token. State this in the FileBounds gate description and gate clause (c).

findings.issue: W17 warp seam claims to 'reuse the EXISTING toLocal (Constellation.vue:145-152) + the host pointerdown already added at :175' — but both are LEXICALLY SCOPED inside the `if (pointerReactive && host && !handle.reducedMotion)` block (lines 144-176). `toLocal` is a local `const` unreachable from the module-scope `defineExpose` at :179, so a `warpTo(clientX, clientY)` method literally cannot reference it as written. And the pointerdown listener is registered ONLY when pointerReactive is on AND not under PRM — so a `warpOnClick` consumer who sets pointerReactive=false gets no click listener at all. The spec PRM-gates warp deliberately (good), but the pointerReactive coupling is unaddressed and the toLocal-reachability is a hard implementation blocker an autonomous agent will hit.
findings.fix: In the W17 Scope §2.5 + FileBounds, instruct the implementer to HOIST `toLocal` (and the canvas-local mapping) out of the `if (pointerReactive...)` block to module/setup scope so both the pointer-web handler and `warpTo` share it, and to register the warp pointerdown listener on a SEPARATE guard `(warpOnClick && host && !handle.reducedMotion)` independent of `pointerReactive` (a consumer may want click-to-warp without the pointer-web). So W04 and W01 describe the SAME shadow/radius behaviour with TWO incompatible mechanisms: W04 says CSS-transition-on-(--dock-motion-resize), W01 says calc()-off-(--dock-morph-t). After W01 lands (W04 dependsOn W01 HARD), W04's premise is false — the transition list it relies on no longer exists.

findings.issue: W42 says the dock 'becomes the FIRST --morph-t instance' (line 211) and useLiquidMorph 'writes a single normalized scalar to --morph-t on elRef' (line 97), with useLayerTransition re-derived as a thin wrapper over useLiquidMorph (line 182). But W42's FileBounds 'Do NOT touch' (lines 192-193) explicitly forbid touching the dock.css morph rules: 'W01 owns the dock.css morph rules + the --dock-morph-t write; W42 generalizes the SCALAR mechanism, it does not re-author the dock CSS.' The dock.css morph rules authored by W01 + extended by W04 + carved into partials by W06 READ --dock-morph-t (~6+ sites). After W42 re-derives the dock wrapper to write --morph-t (the generic name) via useLiquidMorph, the dock.css --dock-morph-t reads become orphaned — they read an unwritten variable. The bridge between the substrate's --morph-t write and the dock.css --dock-morph-t reads is UNSPECIFIED: W42 names neither (a) an alias write (the wrapper writes both --morph-t and --dock-morph-t), (b) a CSS alias (--dock-morph-t: var(--morph-t)), nor (c) a dock.css re-point (forbidden by FileBounds anyway). 'Becomes the first --morph-t instance' is aspirational but does not specify the connection mechanism.
findings.fix: Add an explicit scalar-name-bridge clause to W42 (Scope + the W01 Disjointness section, lines 206-211): state the mechanism by which the dock's --dock-morph-t reads connect to useLiquidMorph's --morph-t write. Recommended (KISS, no FileBounds violation): the dock-flavored useLayerTransition wrapper passes the var NAME to useLiquidMorph (a `varName` option defaulting to --morph-t, the dock passes --dock-morph-t), so the wrapper writes --dock-morph-t directly and the dock.css reads are untouched — '--dock-morph-t IS a --morph-t-protocol scalar by name convention, the substrate writes whichever name the consumer declares.' This keeps W42's 'do not re-author dock.css' invariant intact AND makes 'first --morph-t instance' a precise statement (same protocol, dock-namespaced name). Alternatively state W42 re-points the dock.css reads to --morph-t and REMOVE the FileBounds 'do not touch dock.css' line — but that contradicts W06's settled partials and is the larger churn. Ratify the chosen path at W42 wave-open (it is already a §5.3 ratify decision — fold the naming bridge into that decision).

## §6 — Autonomous-resilience governance (governs every wave)

AX drives END-TO-END, autonomous, over a long-horizon multi-compact session (REQUIREMENTS §21). A
roadblock is NOT a stop. Every wave spec carries the canonical AUTONOMOUS-RESILIENCE CLAUSE below at the
tail of its `## Triumvirate` section; this section states it ONCE as the master template and bounds it.

### §6.1 — The canonical clause (every wave instantiates this verbatim)

> **Autonomous-resilience clause (REQUIREMENTS §22.4b — mandatory, governs this wave's agents under the §21
> autonomous-execution mandate).** A roadblock is a path-forward, not a stop. The implementing agent is
> AUTHORIZED, without waiting for a user prompt, to:
> 1. **Devise an idiomatic GESTALT fix** when the spec-prescribed approach hits a technical roadblock or
>    proves wrong. If the better idiomatic fix stays WITHIN this wave's FileBounds and violates no precept,
>    apply it directly — re-derive from first principles, do not bolt a workaround/legacy/special-case onto
>    the prescribed path (§0; "architectural transpositions for elegance, simplicity, performance are
>    necessary and desirable"). Record the divergence + rationale in the wave's audit JSON.
> 2. **Spawn a tangent triumvirate to work AROUND an error**, never stall. If the fix would expand
>    FileBounds, cross a sibling-wave boundary, re-open a §5.3 ratify decision, or the hard gate fails
>    non-locally / a diagnostic loop hits its third iteration, HALT the failing unit and dispatch the
>    standard triumvirate (ORCHESTRATION §Triumvirate: research → plan-augment carrying the mandatory
>    `## Exact Wave-Amendment Text` → redress; HARD CAPs 20/15/30 min; artefacts
>    `audit/{COHORT}-research|plan|redress.md`). Work the tangent to a resolution, then resume the main
>    line. Do NOT redispatch the failing unit alone; do NOT hand-roll a bespoke recovery shape; do NOT
>    absorb a scope reveal silently.
> 3. **Escalate to the orchestrator ONLY when the decision is genuinely user-gated** — which is the case
>    ONLY when it (i) requires a §21 hard-prohibited action class (financial credentials, account creation,
>    access-control/sharing changes, permanent data deletion, financial trades, security-setting changes,
>    CAPTCHA), (ii) would violate a §21 held invariant (touch `docs/precepts/`; source-embed the
>    `wolfpack-ledger-2026` key; an agent staging/committing/stashing/checking-out the main index;
>    inv-16' writing a dirty sibling tree), or (iii) is a §5.3 ratify-before-drive forcing-function the
>    charter marks USER-ADJUDICATED (W22 Fraunces, W23 glass-scrubber rename, W42 second-consumer).
>    EVERYTHING ELSE — an ambiguous root cause, a wrong-approach roadblock, a non-local gate failure — is
>    resolved autonomously per (1)/(2). On a server throttle or session cap, ScheduleWakeup + resume; never
>    abort. On a cross-session clobber of shared state, coordinate (read the sibling branch/locks), sequence,
>    sleep; never corrupt a sibling tree.

### §6.2 — Insertion contract

The clause sits at the TAIL of every wave's `## Triumvirate` section, directly above `## HardGate`, under ONE
canonical heading: `**Autonomous-resilience clause + triumvirate auto-triggers (per WAVE_SPEC §3a; AX

An autonomous 12-hour run that hits the dirty-sibling wall (LIVE NOW: keyframes.js 37 dirty on tranche-h-impl, value.js 6 dirty, words 23, muster 89) will, under the inherited precept, HALT for arbitration that never comes — the run stalls instead of sleeping/sequencing. The two protocols must be reconciled with an explicit AX override.

findings.issue: No concrete clobber-DETECTION protocol exists for the autonomous run — §21 says 'read its branch/locks' but defines no mechanism. findings.fix: Define the concrete clobber-detection ritual in §21 + coordination/CONSTELLATION.md: BEFORE each integration commit and at each wakeup, the orchestrator runs (a) git fetch origin + compare origin/at-dock-convergence vs the recorded baseline SHA — on a delta, another session pushed: pause, inspect the new commits read-only, rebase the AX line onto them (orchestrator-owned, agents stay read-only per the git clause), re-run gates, resume; (b) check for a .git/index.lock on main and on each sibling (a live lock == a concurrent session mid-write — sleep, retry); (c) re-capture each sibling's HEAD+branch+porcelain and diff against the recorded baseline. The orchestrator (not agents) owns the rebase — the AGENT_DISPATCH_TEMPLATE git clause forbids agents from rebase/fetch-write, so the §21 're-base' language must explicitly scope to the orchestrator.
